description: Add tab bar HTML with 4 tabs (Grid View, Rule Map, Phase Explorer, Light Cones) styled to match the existing dark theme with green accent color
steps: A horizontal tab bar appears between the header and the content area
Exactly 4 tabs are visible: 'Grid View', 'Rule Map', 'Phase Explorer', 'Light Cones'
Tab bar uses the same dark background (#1a1a1a) and green accent (#00ff88) as existing controls
Active tab is visually distinct (green text/border) from inactive tabs (gray)
Tab bar is responsive and does not overflow on narrow screens

description: Implement tab switching JS — clicking a tab shows its content panel, hides all others, and updates the active tab visual state
steps: Clicking any tab shows only that tab's content panel
The previously active panel is hidden (display:none or similar)
The clicked tab gains the active visual state, all others lose it
No flicker or layout shift occurs during tab switch
Only one panel is visible at any given time

description: Wrap the existing grid view (header, controls, grid container) inside a tab panel div so it becomes the content of the 'Grid View' tab
steps: The app loads with 'Grid View' tab active by default
All existing functionality (256 rule cards, mode toggle, density slider, randomize button, modal) works exactly as before
The controls bar and grid container are inside the Grid View panel
No visual regression compared to v1 when on the Grid View tab

description: Create empty placeholder panels for the 3 new tabs (Rule Map, Phase Explorer, Light Cones) with a descriptive loading/placeholder message
steps: Clicking 'Rule Map' tab shows a panel with placeholder content
Clicking 'Phase Explorer' tab shows a panel with placeholder content
Clicking 'Light Cones' tab shows a panel with placeholder content
Each placeholder panel has a title and brief description of what will go there
Switching between all 4 tabs works correctly in any order

description: Add URL hash routing (#grid, #map, #phase, #lightcone) so the selected tab survives page reload
steps: Navigating to the page with #map in the URL opens the Rule Map tab
Navigating with #phase opens Phase Explorer, #lightcone opens Light Cones
Navigating with #grid or no hash opens Grid View (default)
Clicking a tab updates the URL hash without a full page reload
Browser back/forward buttons switch between previously visited tabs

description: Create an SVG scatter plot renderer function that takes a data array of {x, y, label, color} objects and renders circles with axes and gridlines
steps: Function accepts a container element, data array, and config (width, height, margins)
An SVG element is created with correct viewBox dimensions
Data points are rendered as circles at the correct (x, y) positions scaled to the plot area
Horizontal and vertical axes are drawn with gridlines
The plot handles edge cases: empty data, single point, all points at same x or y value
Points with different color values render in different fill colors

description: Add axis labels, tick marks, and value formatting to the scatter plot
steps: X-axis and Y-axis have visible text labels (configurable strings)
Tick marks appear at sensible intervals (5-10 ticks per axis)
Tick values are formatted to appropriate precision (e.g., 0.00 for entropy, 1% for density)
Labels do not overlap with the plot area or get clipped
Tick positions auto-scale based on data range (min/max of actual values)

description: Create an SVG line chart renderer function that takes an array of series [{name, color, points: [{x,y}]}] and renders line paths with axes
steps: Function accepts a container element, series array, and config (width, height, margins)
Each series is rendered as a distinct colored SVG path (no fill, stroke only)
Axes scale to encompass the full range of all series' data
Multiple series can be rendered simultaneously without overlap issues
The chart handles edge cases: empty series, single point series, series with identical values

description: Add legend and series color coding to the line chart
steps: A legend area shows each series' name next to a colored line sample
Legend colors match the actual line colors in the chart
Legend is positioned outside the plot area (top or right) and does not obscure data
Legend handles up to 10 series without visual overflow
Series names are readable and do not truncate

description: Create a Canvas heatmap renderer function that takes a 2D numeric matrix and maps values to a color gradient
steps: Function accepts a canvas element, 2D array (rows x cols), and color config
Values are mapped linearly from min to max across the gradient (e.g., black → cyan → white)
Canvas dimensions match the matrix dimensions with pixelated rendering
A matrix of all zeros renders as uniform minimum color
A matrix of all ones renders as uniform maximum color
Mixed values show a visible gradient between min and max colors

description: Add a color scale bar legend for the heatmap showing the value-to-color mapping
steps: A vertical or horizontal gradient bar is rendered next to the heatmap
The bar shows the full color range from min to max
Min and max values are labeled at the ends of the bar
At least one intermediate tick value is shown
The scale bar matches the actual gradient used in the heatmap

description: Add a hover tooltip system that shows data values on mouseover for scatter plot points and line chart data points
steps: Hovering over a scatter plot circle shows a tooltip with the point's label and x/y values
Hovering over a line chart shows the nearest data point's x/y values
Tooltip appears near the cursor and stays within the SVG bounds
Tooltip disappears when the mouse moves away from the data point
Tooltip text is readable (light text on dark background, matching app theme)

description: Precompute metrics for all 256 rules using center-cell initial config on page load and store in an array for instant access
steps: An array of 256 objects is populated, each containing all 8 existing metrics plus rule number
Computation uses center-cell initial config (deterministic, same result every time)
Metrics use the same 128x128 grid and 128 generations as the card view
The precomputed array is accessible from the Rule Map tab's rendering code
Precomputation does not block the initial page render (runs async or after first paint)

description: Build two dropdown selectors for choosing the X-axis and Y-axis metric (entropy, density, meanField, symmetry, lyapunov, compressibility)
steps: Two <select> dropdowns appear in the Rule Map tab's controls area
Each dropdown lists all available numeric metrics as options
X-axis defaults to 'entropy', Y-axis defaults to 'lyapunov'
Changing either dropdown triggers a re-render of the scatter plot
The 'period' metric is excluded or handled specially since it can be 'aperiodic' (non-numeric)

description: Render scatter plot of all 256 rules using the selected metric pair from the dropdowns
steps: All 256 rules appear as dots on the scatter plot
X positions correspond to the selected X-axis metric values
Y positions correspond to the selected Y-axis metric values
Changing axis selections re-renders the plot with correct positions
The plot auto-scales axes to the actual data range with some padding
Axis labels update to reflect the selected metric names

description: Color-code scatter plot dots by Wolfram class (I=green, II=blue, III=red, IV=orange) and add a class legend
steps: Class I rules appear as green dots
Class II rules appear as blue dots
Class III rules appear as red dots
Class IV rules appear as orange dots
A legend showing all 4 classes with their colors is visible on the plot
Colors match the existing class color scheme from the card view (.class-I through .class-IV)

description: Add hover tooltip on scatter dots showing rule number and both metric values
steps: Hovering over a dot shows 'Rule N' and both metric values with labels
The tooltip includes the Wolfram class of the rule
Tooltip values match the axis labels (e.g., 'Entropy: 0.923, Lyapunov: 1.24')
Tooltip appears near the hovered dot without going off-screen
Moving away from the dot hides the tooltip

description: Wire click on a scatter plot dot to open the existing rule detail modal
steps: Clicking a dot opens the modal with the correct rule's detail view
The modal shows the same 512x512 rendering, truth table, and metrics as when clicking a card
The modal can be closed and the user returns to the Rule Map tab
Clicking different dots opens the correct rule each time
The modal uses center-cell initial config regardless of Grid View mode setting

description: Build rule selector UI with a number input (0-255), increment/decrement buttons, and a 'random rule' button
steps: A number input field accepts values 0-255 in the Phase Explorer tab
Increment (+) and decrement (-) buttons change the value by 1
Increment wraps from 255 to 0, decrement wraps from 0 to 255
A 'Random Rule' button sets the input to a random value 0-255
The input rejects non-numeric values and clamps to 0-255 range
Changing the rule triggers a new density sweep computation

description: Implement density sweep engine — for the selected rule, run 51 density levels (0%, 2%, 4%...100%) and compute all metrics at each level
steps: For the selected rule, 51 separate simulations are run with densities 0.00, 0.02, 0.04, ..., 1.00
Each simulation uses a random initial config at the given density on a 128x128 grid
All existing metrics (entropy, density, meanField, symmetry, lyapunov, compressibility) are computed per density level
Results are stored as an array of 51 objects with density + all metric values
The same random seed approach is used for each density level to reduce noise (seeded PRNG or averaged over 3 runs)

description: Render multi-series line chart with initial density on X-axis and each metric as a separate colored line
steps: X-axis shows density from 0% to 100%
Each metric is plotted as a distinct colored line
The Y-axis auto-scales to accommodate all visible metric values
The chart updates when a new rule is selected and the sweep completes
Lines are smooth and continuous across the 51 data points
Metric names are shown in a legend matching their line colors

description: Add checkboxes to toggle individual metric series visibility on/off in the phase chart
steps: A row of labeled checkboxes appears near the chart, one per metric
All checkboxes are checked (visible) by default
Unchecking a metric hides its line from the chart
Re-checking a metric shows its line again
The Y-axis rescales when series are toggled to fit only visible data
Checkbox label colors match the corresponding line colors

description: Mark critical density points — detect where metric derivatives are steepest and show as vertical dashed lines on the chart
steps: For each visible metric, the density value with the largest absolute derivative is identified
A vertical dashed line is drawn at each critical density on the chart
The dashed line is colored to match the metric it belongs to
A small label near the line shows the density value (e.g., '34%')
Critical lines update when metric visibility is toggled
Rules with no sharp transitions (e.g., Class I) show no critical lines

description: Add chunked async computation with a progress bar to prevent UI freeze during the density sweep
steps: A progress bar is visible while the sweep is running
The progress bar fills from 0% to 100% as density levels are computed
The UI remains responsive during computation (tab switching, scrolling still work)
The chart renders incrementally as results come in, or all at once when complete
Starting a new sweep (changing rule) cancels any in-progress sweep
The progress bar disappears when computation is complete

description: Implement block frequency counter — given a row array, count occurrences of all length-L binary patterns for L=1..8
steps: Function accepts a binary row (array of 0/1) and block length L
Returns a Map or object mapping each L-length binary pattern to its count
For L=1, counts of 0s and 1s match a simple tally of the row
For L=2, the 4 patterns (00, 01, 10, 11) are counted correctly with wrap-around
Total count of all patterns equals the row length (sliding window with wrap)
Works correctly for L=8 (256 possible patterns) on a 128-cell row

description: Implement H(L) computation — Shannon entropy from block frequencies, averaged across all rows of the spacetime grid
steps: For each row in the grid, block frequencies at length L are computed and Shannon entropy calculated
The per-row entropies are averaged to produce H(L)
H(1) matches or closely approximates the existing computeEntropy function
H(L) is computed for L=1 through L=8, producing an array of 8 values
H(L) is monotonically non-decreasing (H(L+1) >= H(L))
For a grid of all zeros, H(L) = 0 for all L

description: Implement entropy rate h estimation — compute as H(L) - H(L-1) for the largest L values, or as the slope of a linear fit to H(L) vs L
steps: Entropy rate h is computed from the H(L) array
h is approximated as the average of H(L) - H(L-1) for L=6,7,8 (converged region)
For a completely random grid, h is close to 1.0 (1 bit per cell)
For a periodic/static grid (e.g., Rule 0), h is close to 0.0
h is always non-negative
Value is returned as a single float

description: Implement excess entropy E — compute as the y-intercept of the linear extrapolation of H(L) vs L from the converged region
steps: Excess entropy E is derived from H(L) and the entropy rate h
E is computed as the average of (H(L) - h*L) for large L values
For a completely random grid, E is close to 0 (no structure beyond randomness)
For a structured/complex rule (e.g., Rule 110), E is positive and measurably different from random rules
E is always non-negative (or clamp to 0 if numerical noise makes it slightly negative)
Value is returned as a single float

description: Integrate blockEntropy (H(L) array), entropyRate, and excessEntropy into the computeAllMetrics return object
steps: computeAllMetrics now returns blockEntropy (array of 8 floats), entropyRate (float), and excessEntropy (float)
Existing metrics (entropy, density, meanField, etc.) are unchanged
All 256 rules' cards still render correctly with the expanded metrics object
The precomputed metrics array for the Rule Space Map includes the new fields
No performance regression — adding block entropy computation does not noticeably slow card rendering

description: Display entropy rate and excess entropy on rule cards and in the modal metrics table
steps: Each rule card's metrics area shows entropy rate (e.g., 'h: 0.834')
Each rule card's metrics area shows excess entropy (e.g., 'E: 0.12')
The modal metrics table includes rows for 'Entropy Rate' and 'Excess Entropy' with 4 decimal places
Values are consistent between card and modal for the same rule
Class III rules show high entropy rate (~1.0) and low excess entropy (~0.0)
Class IV rules show moderate entropy rate and higher excess entropy than Class III

description: Add H(L) vs L line plot in the modal detail view showing the block entropy curve with annotated entropy rate slope and excess entropy intercept
steps: A small line chart appears in the modal showing H(L) on Y-axis, L (1-8) on X-axis
The 8 data points are plotted and connected with a line
A dashed line showing the linear fit (slope = h, intercept = E) is overlaid
The entropy rate h and excess entropy E values are annotated on the chart
The chart is labeled 'Block Entropy' and fits within the modal layout
The chart uses the same dark theme styling as the rest of the app

description: Build rule selector and flip position controls — rule number input and cell position selector with center-cell default
steps: A rule number input (0-255) with +/- buttons appears in the Light Cones tab
A cell position input or slider allows choosing which cell to flip (0 to width-1)
Default flip position is the center cell (cell 64 for 128-wide grid)
Both controls validate input ranges and reject invalid values
Changing either control triggers a new perturbation computation
A 'Random Rule' button is available for quick exploration

description: Implement perturbation engine — run original and single-cell-flipped grids, compute the absolute difference matrix
steps: Original grid is generated with center-cell initial config for the selected rule
Perturbed grid is generated with one additional cell flipped at the selected position
A difference matrix is computed: diff[y][x] = |original[y][x] - perturbed[y][x]|
The difference matrix has the same dimensions as the grids (128x128)
For Rule 0 (all cells die), the difference matrix is all zeros after generation 1
For Rule 30 (chaotic), the difference matrix shows an expanding cone of 1s

description: Render the difference matrix as a Canvas heatmap using the heatmap charting primitive (0=black, 1=bright cyan/green)
steps: The difference matrix is rendered on a canvas with pixelated rendering
Cells where original equals perturbed (diff=0) are black
Cells where original differs from perturbed (diff=1) are a bright color (cyan or green)
The heatmap has the same pixel-art aesthetic as the existing CA grid renders
The canvas is sized appropriately within the Light Cones tab panel
A color scale bar is shown indicating 0 (no difference) to 1 (different)

description: Estimate propagation speed — at each generation find the leftmost and rightmost differing cells and compute the cone slope in cells per generation
steps: For each row (generation) in the difference matrix, the leftmost and rightmost non-zero cells are found
The spread width (rightmost - leftmost) is tracked over generations
Propagation speed is computed as the average rate of spread increase per generation
Speed is expressed in cells/generation (e.g., 1.0 means the cone expands by 1 cell per side per step)
Maximum possible speed is 1.0 cell/generation (the light speed of ECA)
Periodic boundary wrap-around is handled correctly when the cone reaches grid edges

description: Display propagation speed metric and cone angle alongside the heatmap
steps: Propagation speed is shown as a labeled value next to the heatmap (e.g., 'Speed: 0.87 cells/gen')
Cone angle is derived from speed and displayed (e.g., 'Cone angle: 41°')
A qualitative label is shown: 'maximal' for speed ~1.0, 'moderate' for 0.3-0.7, 'localized' for <0.3, 'none' for 0
Values update when the rule or flip position changes
For Class I rules (converge to uniform), speed shows as 0 or near-0
For Class III rules (chaotic), speed shows as close to 1.0

description: Add 'compare two rules' mode — show two light cone heatmaps side-by-side for visual comparison
steps: A toggle or button switches between single-rule and comparison mode
In comparison mode, two rule selectors are visible (Rule A and Rule B)
Two heatmaps render side-by-side with equal dimensions
Each heatmap has its own propagation speed and cone angle displayed below it
Rule labels are clearly shown above each heatmap (e.g., 'Rule 30' vs 'Rule 110')
Both heatmaps use the same flip position for a fair comparison
